newsitem.title: RUSSIA: OSCE office robbed in breakaway Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: OSCE office robbed in breakaway Chechnya.

text.p: Thieves on Wednesday robbed the office of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), the interior minister of Russia's breakaway Chechnya region said.

"The attack, which took place early this morning, resulted in the theft of various valuables and technical equipment," Kazbek Makhashev told Reuters, adding that a security guard had also gone missing.
Itar-Tass news agency, quoting Chechnya's general prosecutor, said the thieves had stolen around $30,000.

Makhashev, whose ministry has been struggling to combat a wave of lawlessness sweeping the Caucasus region since the end of its war with Russia, said police had identified the thieves and were confident of catching them in the near future.
He ruled out any possible political motives for the robbery, which he described as "a regular criminal incident".

The OSCE has played a key role in peace negotiations in Chechnya, helping to seal a deal last August ending 21 months of fighting between local rebels and Russian troops in which tens of thousands of people were killed.
It also helped to organise Chechnya's presidential and parliamentary elections in January which brought former guerrilla chief Aslan Maskhadov to power.

But endemic lawlessness has been frustrating Chechnya's efforts to restore its shattered economy. Hostage-taking has become an acute problem and this month alone two Britons, one Frenchman and a Slovak have been kidnapped in and around Chechnya by different groups of gunmen seeking ransoms.
